correctness.rationale: The coefficient recurrence gives the exact sum S_k=(2k+1)a_k. After summation by parts, bounded variation of sqrt(t)*exp(wt) on [0,1] and the summed O((k+1)^(-1/2)) coefficient errors give P_n(exp(w/n))/sqrt(n)=H(w)+O_R(1/n) uniformly on every fixed disk |w|<=R. For Re w<=0 and Im w>0, integration by parts of the sine integral against (1-cos(yt))/y gives a nonnegative endpoint term and a strictly positive integral, because t^(-1/2)*exp(Re(w)t) is strictly decreasing; the term at zero vanishes like t^(3/2). Conjugation and positivity on the real axis finish exclusion. Zero-free exponential type would force H to be an exponential of a linear polynomial, incompatible with H(-R) comparable to R^(-1/2). The differential identity H+2wH'=2exp(w)/sqrt(pi) gives simplicity. The oscillatory term in bounded real-part strips is the nonzero leading Fresnel term exp(i sign(y) pi/4)/sqrt(|y|): subtracting the weight at zero gives an absolutely integrable derivative for the remainder and an O(1/|y|) bound. Thus a zero exists and c_* is a strictly positive attained minimum. Global angular exclusion is decisive: with d_k=a_(k-1)-a_k one has (1-z)P_n(z)=Q_n(z)-a_n*z^(n+1), where Q_n is the truncation of sqrt(1-z). Its unit-circle error is bounded by a_n. At z=rho*u in the candidate collar, rho^k-1<=k(rho-1)rho^(k-1) and sum(k*d_k)=S_(n-1)/2=O(sqrt(n)), so Q_n(rho*u)-Q_n(u)=O_C(n^(-1/2)). At a zero this forces sqrt(|1-u|)=O_C(n^(-1/2)) and a bounded scaled logarithm. Strict coefficient ratios exclude all |z|<=1. Rouché on a circle of radius M/n at a simple minimizing H zero gives a candidate, and on the resulting fixed compact set of possible scaled nearest roots the pointwise bound |H|=O(1/n) forces distance O(1/n) to a simple H zero. Exponentiating yields the claimed O(n^(-2)) radial remainder on both sides. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; its Newton solves follow one local branch, and the polynomial coefficient recurrence also uses a Python floating ratio before multiplying the high-precision values. Neither that computation nor a certified numerical value of c_* is needed.

originality.rationale: The supported contribution is the global minimum-modulus asymptotic and its remainder for the precise central-binomial section sequence, not local scaling or an error-function zero in isolation. The same problem appears in Technau with a logarithmic gap, and the available nearby section and incomplete-beta results do not give the uniform complex collar localization needed for the global minimum. The historical priority check is bounded; unresolved same-family older sources are named below without assigning them a noncoverage verdict.
residual_risks: Love (1949) and Talbot Brunel TR/46 were not lawfully accessible for independent full-text comparison. In particular a prior same-family root asymptotic in either would affect historical priority. The positive decision rests on actual available comparisons, not on inaccessibility.
No certification is given of the indexed minimizing zero of H, nor of an exhaustive check of older section-zero literature.

value.rationale: It resolves Technau’s explicit nearest-zero asymptotic question for a classical family by removing the full logarithmic uncertainty, gives a strictly positive well-defined sharp constant, and improves the radial remainder to second order. The proof isolates why local scaling captures the true global minimum, a useful distinction in section-zero problems. It is not a claim to solve the larger Shapiro coefficient problem or to numerically certify the identity of the extremizing zero.
